description: Captured documents (07 C.0 #5, C.2): Email and Attachment from the versioned mail capture (integrations/capture_mail.py, source graph_mail, cited graph-mail://), SharePointFile from the versioned SharePoint capture (integrations/capture_sharepoint.py, source sharepoint, cited sharepoint://<drive>/<item>@<eTag>). Documents are evidence, never business truth by themselves; every reader is re-gated per mailbox (audience mail:<mailbox>) or per SharePoint item (audience sharepoint:<drive>, then the item's path keys and permissions recorded at capture). Mentions of identifiers in a document are stored lead links (Email.mentions_<type>, Attachment.mentions_<type> from an attachment's own extracted text, a PDF cited by page, and SharePointFile.mentions_<type>, binding kind mention, written by ontology/mentions.py into the same store generation); the loader generates one such link type per served type with an identifier property from one rule per document type (ontology/schema.py MENTION_LINK_RULES, evidence wb.mentions and ctx.mentions below); ambiguous candidates are kept, never merged. Copies: an Email's internet_message_id (with equal headers and body preview, so a forged Message-ID groups nothing) and a captured file's content_sha256 are verified identifier kinds whose equal values name copies (ontology/schema/identifiers.json copies): one message in several mailboxes, one file attached, stored or packed in a container. A copy identity is never read from text, so no mention link type targets a document type (ontology/schema.py mention_links). Copies stay separate objects with their own permissions; evidence they carry counts once (ontology/mentions.py confirmation_support).

object_types.description: One captured mail message version (Graph immutable id + changeKey). Source text is untrusted; the body is cited (row.body_text) but not projected as a value.

bindings.note: One object per message (mailbox object id + immutable message id); one version per captured changeKey interval (MailCaptureStore.messages).

properties.name: sender
properties.description: The From address as Graph reports it (no SPF/DKIM).

properties.name: internet_message_id
properties.description: One message delivered to several mailboxes: one object per mailbox copy, one Message-ID. Verified (the sending server writes it) but not unique: copies are candidates of one another, never merged; evidence they carry counts once (ontology/mentions.py confirmation_support).

object_types.description: One captured file attachment of one message version, byte-pinned (graph-mail://...#attachment=<id>&sha256=<hex>). Attachments whose bytes were not captured have no handle and are not projected. Removed with its message, it is marked missing_from_source_since like the message.

properties.name: content_sha256
properties.description: Equal bytes: an attachment and any other captured file with its digest are copies, never merged; evidence they carry counts once (ontology/mentions.py confirmation_support).

object_types.description: One captured SharePoint drive item version, keyed by (driveId, itemId) and cited sharepoint://<drive>/<item>@<eTag> (#sha256=<hex> names the pinned bytes). Name, path and extracted text are untrusted source text; the text is cited (row.content_text) but not projected as a value. A file whose bytes were not captured (over the size cap, or unreadable) is still a version, with content_status saying why: incomplete, never absent.

bindings.note: One object per drive item (drive id + item id); one version per captured eTag interval (SharePointCaptureStore); a move keeps the object (same item id) and opens a new interval at the new path.

properties.name: content_sha256
properties.description: Equal bytes: a SharePoint file and any other captured file with its digest are copies, never merged; evidence they carry counts once (ontology/mentions.py confirmation_support).

properties.name: content_status
properties.description: captured, exceeds_cap or unavailable:<detail> (retried by later captures).

properties.name: portal_metadata
properties.description: What the Portal states in this version's own SharePoint listItem columns (stated-by-Portal, never a Workbench proposal): every Portal-taxonomy column of operating/doc_metadata_taxonomy.py COLUMNS once, filled ones under columns, absent (empty_or_not_provisioned: Graph omits an empty column), blank, unread or unsupported ones under gaps, cited to the listItem (citation.source_api, list_item_id, drive_etag). Read GET-only per version and bound to its eTag (taxonomy.stated_metadata); null when no snapshot of this version was read. A Ref column's record number is a mention of the file (SharePointFile.mentions_<type>). Never written to SharePoint.

properties.name: document_kind
properties.description: The Workbench document kind a person confirmed for these bytes (operating/playbook_originals.py KINDS: ao_scan, proforma_invoice, ...); never a SharePoint column. Reviewed by a person, never inferred.

sources.note: Written by the kind-confirmation projection step (operating/kind_confirmation.py projection_step), not read from the capture: a person's current confirmation of this file (plx.document_fields mode request), bound to the same drive item, eTag and bytes (this path), valid from its confirmation until a later one supersedes it; lineage workbench.

properties.name: document_category
properties.description: The Portal DocumentCategory (portal/src/lib/storage/folder-taxonomy.ts) a person confirmed for these bytes: findable with plx.find object_type SharePointFile and a filter on it. A proposal for the SharePoint column, never written to SharePoint.

sources.note: Written by the kind-confirmation projection step (operating/kind_confirmation.py projection_step), not read from the capture: a person's current confirmation of this file (plx.document_fields mode request), bound to the same drive item, eTag and bytes (this path), valid from its confirmation until a later one supersedes it; lineage workbench.

properties.name: proposed_portal_metadata
properties.description: Every Portal-taxonomy column a person confirmed for these bytes (DocumentType, DocumentCategory, PartyRef, ...), the confirmed document kind and the confirmation id and time, as proposed SharePoint metadata: status proposed, written_to_sources false. The Workbench never writes it to SharePoint or the Portal.

sources.note: Written by the kind-confirmation projection step (operating/kind_confirmation.py projection_step), not read from the capture: a person's current confirmation of this file (plx.document_fields mode request), bound to the same drive item, eTag and bytes (this path), valid from its confirmation until a later one supersedes it; lineage workbench.

object_types.description: One member of a captured container file (a zip that is not an Office package, an .eml or an Outlook .msg; a mail attachment or a SharePoint file), nested containers recursively, cited <container handle>&member=<path>&member_sha256=<hex> (the member's own bytes inside the container's pinned bytes). Its text is the one reading of its bytes (integrations/captured_text.py) and is cited (row.content_text), never projected as a value. A member the extractor could not read (state unread, reason text_<status>) and every part of the container's structure that was not read (an encrypted or over-cap member, an undecoded .msg property: state unread or skipped_by_cap with its reason or cap) is a member too: a visible gap, never omitted. Same audience and validity interval as its container; every reader is gated by the container.

bindings.note: One object per member path of a captured zip/.msg/.eml attachment (ontology/project_graph.py member_records); one version per attachment version.
One object per member path of a captured zip/.msg/.eml drive item (ontology/project_graph.py member_records); one version per drive item version.

properties.name: path
properties.description: The member's path inside its container (nested containers joined by !/); untrusted source text.

properties.name: state
properties.description: read, container (its own members follow), unread (reason) or skipped_by_cap (reason names the cap).

properties.name: reason
properties.description: Why the member or part was not read: text_<extractor status> for a member file, else the part accounting reason (operating/use_case_parts.py REASONS) or cap.

properties.name: kind
properties.description: file for a member file, else the kind of the part not read (operating/use_case_parts.py KINDS).

properties.name: content_sha256
properties.description: SHA-256 of the member's bytes (null for a part read without bytes). Equal bytes: a member and any other captured file with its digest are copies, never merged; evidence they carry counts once (ontology/mentions.py confirmation_support).

link_types.name: attached_to
link_types.description: The message an attachment was captured with (Graph structure: the attachment's message id; Graph immutable ids are unique across mailboxes, and a key that ever named two messages makes the link an ambiguous lead, never a guess).

link_types.name: in_attachment
link_types.description: The captured mail attachment a member was read from (the attachment id copied from the container record; Graph attachment ids embed their message's, and a key that ever named two attachments makes the link an ambiguous lead, never a guess).

link_types.name: in_file
link_types.description: The captured SharePoint file a member was read from (the drive item id copied from the container record).

link_types.name: sent_by_supplier
link_types.description: The Supplier whose party sent this message: the sender address scored against the supplier's website domain, its name and a BC contact holding the address (ontology/identity_scoring.py mail_sender). Reviewed only: no score links a message by itself.

link_types.name: sent_by_customer
link_types.description: The Customer whose party sent this message: the sender address scored against the customer's name and a BC contact holding the address (ontology/identity_scoring.py mail_sender). Reviewed only: no score links a message by itself.

event_types.description: The message arrived in the captured mailbox (Graph receivedDateTime).

wb.capture_mail.note: MailCaptureStore: one row per message version interval keyed by graph-mail://<mailbox>/<message>@<changeKey>; attachments byte-pinned; per-reader mailbox audience.

wb.capture_sharepoint.note: SharePointCaptureStore: one row per drive-item version interval keyed by sharepoint://<drive>/<item>@<eTag>; bytes and extracted text byte-pinned; per-reader path keys and item permissions recorded at capture.

wb.graph_read_drive.note: GET-only SharePoint drive reader record (drive_id, id, eTag, name, path, size, mime_type, last_modified).

wb.mentions.note: Identifier mentions extracted by the one identifier grammar and resolved through the identifier index; stored as lead links (store_mention_links).

ctx.documents.note: Document interface (Email, Attachment, SharePointFile); Document attached_to Email.

ctx.mentions.note: Document mentions any object: mention resolution (lead/corroborated).

wb.kind_confirmation.note: KindConfirmations: a person's confirmation of an original's document kind and Portal-taxonomy columns (MCP elicitation form), in the Workbench's own store; projection_step writes the current one onto the SharePointFile version with the same item, eTag and bytes.

wb.container_members.note: member_records / member_documents: the members of captured zip/.msg/.eml files through operating/use_case_parts.py members and integrations/captured_text.py container_members; unread parts are member records with their reason.

wb.identity_scoring.note: Weighted identity candidates (Fellegi-Sunter: blocking, field comparison levels, m/u from verified and reviewed pairs) offered for a person's review; a link exists only once plx.review records the decision, projected by ontology/reviews.py link_step as reviewed.
